responses.response: Diagnose the first error first. In this workspace, `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4` defines `Container_Webapp`, `Container_Spa`, and `Container_Api`, but not `Container_WebUi`, so that kind name is definitely invalid. Because an element declared with an unknown kind does not resolve correctly, `Element not found: api` is often a cascade from the failed declaration. Clean sequence: fix or define the kind first, then re-check `api`; if it still fails, verify that `api` is the real alias and that you are using the correct scope/FQN, for example `system.api` when you are outside the parent block.

The real cause is the view scope, not `rank same` by itself. `system -> system.api` treats a parent and its child as if they were peers in a dynamic interaction, which is really containment, not a proper scenario step. Then `rank same user, system.api` tries to align an external peer with a nested child, exposing the same hierarchy problem. Fix the view by choosing one abstraction level: either keep it at system level (`user -> system`) or switch to container level and model peer interactions such as `user -> system.webapp` and `system.webapp -> system.api`; use `rank same` only for peers in that chosen level.

Diagnose the two errors separately, in order. `sends` is definitely wrong for this workspace: `projects/shared/spec-global.c4` defines model relationships `uses`, `calls`, `async`, `reads`, and `writes`, while `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4` defines deployment relationships like `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `amqp`, `redis`, and `sql`; `sends` exists in neither set. `dataLayer.cache` may also be wrong, but that is a separate check: confirm the exact alias chain used in the model, because FQNs must match the declared aliases and scope exactly. So the proper diagnosis is: first replace `sends` with the intended defined relationship, then verify whether `dataLayer.cache` is the real FQN or whether you need a different path such as a fuller parent-qualified name.

The root cause is that the same traffic was modeled twice at two different abstraction levels, and the protocol name was put in the wrong vocabulary once. In this workspace, `https` is a deployment/infrastructure relationship from `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4`, while model relationships are `uses/calls/async/reads/writes` from `projects/shared/spec-global.c4`. The cheat sheet also says to put interaction technology on the system-model relationship and to use deployment relationships only for infrastructure-specific connections. Clean fix: keep the logical app-to-app interaction once in `model {}` with a model relationship such as `calls` plus `technology 'HTTPS'`, let deployed instances inherit that via `instanceOf`, and only add a separate deployment `https` edge when it represents a distinct infrastructure hop rather than the same application traffic repeated.
